threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can tell a newbie by how they still struggle to differentiate between the 30 bus and the 149. Regulars know which one to catch at night.
Last night on the N35, a bloke started singing opera loudly. Half the bus joined in. Never thought I'd see that at 2 AM in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard the old Turkish shopkeeper gossiping about the latest BVG strikes at the corner café, while the kids played football right in the street.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night Döner stand that doubles as an art gallery, showcasing local artists while you wait for your kebab.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they react when BART delays hit—no complaints, just a resigned chuckle about the inevitable chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 today, driver stopped mid-ride to explain to a guy why he can’t bring his skateboard on. Classic Tenderloin moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves tapas. In Gràcia, you’ll find places dishing out hearty platillos that are anything but typical.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still call it ‘La Rambla’ with the emphasis on the 'la,' not realizing it’s just ‘Rambla’ to the locals.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the bus' means the double-decker. Wait till you try the old banger routes in spots that barely have a stop.
Overheard a couple arguing on the 45, she claimed he never lets her pick the takeaway. He said he only ordered what she wanted last week. Classic Brixton bustle.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a child casually say 'Wagenburg' as if it was the local playground, I knew I was really part of the Neukölln vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the BVG announcements sound more like a DJ set? It's an art form, especially when they mix in those delay effects during the strikes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A local will complain about the 14 Mission being late, while a newcomer just waits without questioning it. The eye-roll says it all.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a free ride last New Year’s Eve. Watching a guy juggle while the bus crawled through the rain felt perfectly San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the nightlife; they miss the quiet mornings where locals cherish their café con leche and a good book at La Pepita.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to sit anywhere but the busy terraces, fully embracing the sun while ignoring the chill of the evening.
